answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can give each identity a kernel of earned reputation that mirrors its real transaction history: new agents begin with near-zero standing and must complete small, verifiable jobs before handling valuable trades. Every completed job adds a signed receipt, so a fresh fake identity shows an empty mirror. To look trustworthy, an attacker must fund thousands of identities through months of real work and staked deposits, and even a small delta in detected fraud wipes out that standing, making forgery cost more than any fake identity can earn.
